title: Obserra PCI DSS Purchase-Stream Crosswalk
scopeStatement: Obserra redirects customers to Stripe-hosted checkout and does not collect or store primary account numbers, card verification codes, PIN data, or magnetic-stripe data in application code. This crosswalk documents implementation evidence and does not constitute PCI certification, an SAQ determination, or an assessor attestation.

controls.capability: Payment entry is delegated to Stripe-hosted checkout; Obserra purchase routes do not render card-entry components or accept raw card data.
Checkout and webhook processing fail closed when required Stripe credentials or webhook secrets are unavailable.
Application code does not persist sensitive authentication data or cardholder account numbers; only bounded purchase, entitlement, and provider reference metadata is processed.
Payment collection and provider API communication use Stripe-hosted HTTPS endpoints and Vercel-managed TLS transport.
Purchase-stream changes are subject to source review, dependency analysis, security gates, end-to-end validation, and rollback evidence.
Hosted checkout reduces payment-page attack surface while purchase endpoints enforce bounded metadata, controlled redirects, and provider-side payment capture.
Administrative billing and payment-management operations require authenticated identity, owner authorization where applicable, and recent reverification.
Passwordless authentication, passkeys, verified email methods, enterprise SSO, and strict step-up controls protect sensitive payment-administration functions.
Payment events are logged using provider event IDs, bounded purchase references, fulfillment state, and course identifiers without card data or provider secrets.
Purchase-stream failures, fulfillment outcomes, deployment health, and compliance evidence are continuously surfaced through operational and governance dashboards.
Payment routes, webhooks, dependencies, runtime behavior, and deployed customer journeys are included in release-blocking security and regression testing.
AI-assisted patch proposals for purchase systems require impact assessment, security analysis, preview validation, approval according to risk, rollback planning, and immutable evidence.
